title.rendered: Africa’s beverage market gets intelligence platform

content.rendered:
Africa’s beverage industry is set to receive its first dedicated intelligence platform as Drinkabl Africa launches the New Pour Summit 2026 to help brands navigate economic volatility and unlock growth opportunities across the continent.

The summit, scheduled for 25 July 2026, will be held in a hybrid format at the Golden Tulip Westlands in Nairobi, Kenya, and online under the theme, ‘Liquid Resilience: Future-Proofing Beverage Brands in Africa’s VUCA Markets’.

In a webinar on Monday, the Co-Convener of the New Pour Summit and Co-Founder of Drinkabl Africa, Tosin Balogun, said the initiative will address the lack of structured market intelligence and storytelling in Africa’s beverage sector despite its multi-billion-dollar value.

“Africa’s beverage industry is a multi-billion-dollar sector, yet it has no structured storytelling machinery behind it. Drinkabl Africa and The New Pour Summit are the first to change that,” Balogun said.

He added that the platform was designed to provide practical business solutions rather than theoretical discussions: “Our mandate is simple: every delegate should leave on Saturday with at least one insight they can implement in their business on Monday.”

According to the organisers, the summit will unveil the New Pour Report, which aggregates insights from more than 10 independent publications, tracks capital flows into the Global South with a focus on Africa, identifies 10 major industry trends and provides a growth playbook for founders and operators.

The programme will also feature artificial intelligence tools for advertising testing and real-time consumer insights, alongside sessions on strategy, distribution, innovation, capital, branding and consumer trends.

Balogun said African beverage companies is facing increasing pressure from currency volatility, distribution bottlenecks, regulatory changes and counterfeiting, making access to reliable market intelligence more important.

“The brands that will thrive will not necessarily be the biggest, but the most informed,” Balogun said.

Industry expert Walter Serem said brands must tailor their strategies to African markets instead of replicating global models.

“Positioning is integral. It’s about being something for someone, not everything for everyone. We need deeper conversations on cultural context. A Red Bull strategy cannot just be copied in Africa, it must be localised,” Serem said.

Balogun said the organisers planned to expand the New Pour Summit beyond an annual conference into a year-round platform connecting beverage companies, investors and market data to support the industry’s long-term growth.

“This is not a flash in the pan. Our commitment is to keep refining this platform to serve Africans and the global market, and to contribute to the growth of Africa’s beverage industry,” Balogun said.
